extracted.intended_audience: doctors, medical researchers, and the general public interested in medical evidence
extracted.subtask_description: A TEDMED 2012 talk (Ben Goldacre) summarizing the problem of unpublished negative or inconclusive clinical trial results and the dangers this poses for doctors and medical research. The page is a public-facing talk summary and transcript pointer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish all clinical trial results (including negative/inconclusive)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a new drug gets tested, the results of the trials should be published for the rest of the medical world -- except much of the time, negative or inconclusive findings go unreported, leaving doctors and researchers in the dark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unreported negative or inconclusive findings are especially misleading and dangerous because they bias the evidence base that doctors use to prescribe drugs; transparency requires full reporting of trial outcomes so clinicians and researchers can make informed decisions.
